Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + asks so we can model the pricing and propose a pilot: 

Summary from demo:
- Scope: BrightBank conversational assistant (customer support) + internal KB lookups. Expecting mixed prompts: short intents + long context retrieval.
- Target launch: Q3 pilot (2–4 week pilot then scale).

Requests we need from you to finalize the unit-cost estimate:
1) Estimated monthly token volume (rough): daily active calls, avg tokens per call, monthly tokens. If you only have ranges that's fine.
2) Target effective unit cost goal (you mentioned a target $/1M tokens during the demo). Confirm a target so we can back into cache/quantization choices.
3) Any retention / privacy constraints for cached prefixes (TTL, PII policy) — this affects whether we can use shared public cache or customer-isolated cache.

Assumptions we will model (and please flag changes):
- Base model pricing (raw, no cache): $1,200 per 1M tokens (reference for this proposal).
- Two cache modes: shared prefix cache (improves hit rate but shared across customers) vs customer-only prefix cache.
- Default TTL for prefixes we propose: 30 days (evict older prefixes automatically).

Attachments: RBW_prefix_cache_model.xlsx (live sensitivity table) and SOW-draft-v1.pdf (pilot scope + timeline).

Next steps I propose: 
- You send the volume estimate + target $/1M by EOD Wed.
- Ben will run a quick sensitivity model and return an effective $/1M for 3 hit-rate scenarios (30/55/70%).
- If numbers look ok, we propose a 2-week pilot to measure actual hit rate on a 10k-session sample.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call if you want to walk the spreadsheet together.

Alex / team —

I ran the sensitivity curves in the attached RBW_prefix_cache_model.xlsx against the numbers you gave. High-level takeaway: with our baseline model price of $1,200 / 1M tokens (no cache) the effective $/1M after caching looks like this under our prefix caching assumptions: 

Assumptions I used (documented in sheet):
- Avg tokens / session: 150 (prompt + generation)
- Prefix cache saves ~60% of prompt tokens on a hit (we only charge generation tokens on a hit in this model)
- Hit-rate scenarios: 30%, 55%, 70%
- Customer-isolated cache gives same hit-rate curve but with slightly higher infra surcharge (+5%) due to isolation.

Results (effective $ per 1M tokens):
- 30% hit: effective $/1M = $840
- 55% hit: effective $/1M = $540
- 70% hit: effective $/1M = $420

Explanation (short): the base cost assumes we bill per token consumed by the model. On a prefix-cache hit we avoid re-sending the full prompt; that reduces billed tokens and therefore lowers the effective $/1M. The customer-only cache surcharge moves the $/1M up roughly 5–8% depending on utilization.

Pilot recommendation:
- Run 2-week pilot over a 10k-session sample. Track actual prefix reuse, PII flag rate, and observed hit-rate. If your observed hit-rate is >=55% we can justify a quoted effective unit price near $500–$600 / 1M.
- Technical notes: we need a sampling window (we recommend 2 weeks) and a flag in your telemetry to mark sessions that must not be cached (PII).

I attached the workbook with the scenario table and a one-page SOW draft. Will update numbers if you confirm avg tokens and whether you'd take customer-isolated cache.

--

If these are straightforward I think we can move ahead and share the 10k-session sample under the addendum.

Alex — thanks for the governance questions; short answers and next steps below.

Short answers: 
- TTL / eviction: per-namespace TTL is supported in Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted default is global TTL but we can configure rule-based TTL (e.g., TTL=24h for intent X) as part of the pilot.
- PII detection & disabling cache: we provide an opt-in telemetry flag to mark sessions as "do-not-cache" and built-in regex/ML PII detectors that can auto-block caching for flagged inputs. For absolute control we recommend customer-isolated cache for any traffic containing sensitive identifiers.
- Audit logs: yes — the pilot SOW includes token-level logs showing cache hits/misses and eviction events (obfuscated tokens for privacy). We will provide the logs to your compliance team under the NDA addendum.

Concrete next steps: 
1) Alex -> share 10k-session sample + indicate whether sensitive sessions should be pre-marked.
2) I will update the SOW with an option for per-namespace TTL and customer-isolated cache (small infra surcharge).
3) Ben -> run pilot modeling with both shared and isolated cache columns and return a revised effective $/1M (sheet + short commentary) by EOD Wed.
4) We'll draft the NDA addendum and the pilot amendment for signature.

If that timeline works I'll send the updated SOW and a calendar invite for a 30-min kickoff next week.

Thanks,
